Done. The export succeeded on the first execution and passed an independent bit-exact re-verification.

**What I did**

- Wrote `out/T3/solution.py`, a plain torch plus safetensors script. It builds the 64 projection names and 48 buffer names explicitly from templates, so no regex can overreach onto embeddings, norms, or the real `attention.dense.bias` parameters.
- Casts the 64 matrices to bfloat16, upcasts every other kept tensor to float32, and drops the 48 buffers.
- Enforces the four required checks before any file is written, plus a key-set check and a float32 count check. Failure exits non-zero.
- Shards greedily under the 256 MiB tensor-data budget and writes a HuggingFace-style index file with a full weight map.

**Result**

| Item | Value |
|---|---|
| Executions | 1, no failures |
| Shards | 9 |
| Tensors | 196, of which 64 bfloat16 and 132 float32 |
| Embeddings | 412 MB each after upcast, so each sits alone in its own shard |

The verification pass reloaded every shard, compared each tensor against a fresh cast of the input with exact equality, and confirmed the index maps every tensor to the file that holds it and that no multi-tensor shard exceeds the budget.

One note for the task text: it quotes the embeddings as 206 MB, which is their float16 size. They are twice that in float32, which still forces them into their own shards, so the outcome is unchanged. The self-report is in `out/T3/REPORT.md`.
